Tests on models and real readings show CAAL beating standard baselines.
arxiv-2602-12125:
On-policy distillation aligns a student with a teacher's outputs on the student's own trajectories, often beating off-policy distillation and reinforcement learning. Wenkai Yang and five co-authors first show theoretically that it is a special case of dense KL-constrained reinforcement learning with reward and regularization weighted equally.

Their generalized framework adds a flexible reference model and a reward scaling factor. Scaling reward above one, called reward extrapolation, consistently improves over standard distillation and can even let the student surpass its teachers when merging domain experts. In strong-to-weak distillation, choosing the teacher's pre-reinforcement-learning base model as reference further sharpens the reward signal, at the cost of needing that variant and extra compute.
arxiv-2602-12325:
Early supermassive black holes pose a growth puzzle: how did they get so massive so soon? Qinyue Fei led a large team here, studying GNz7q, a red, X-ray-weak quasar in a dusty starburst galaxy at redshift 7.19, with JWST and NOEMA data. Broad Balmer lines confirm a super-Eddington black hole of about 35 million suns, using accretion-corrected mass estimates.

After removing the point source, stellar light reveals a host of about 32 billion suns in stars, forming stars at roughly 330 suns per year. The pair sits on the local black hole to stellar mass relation, and both are growing fast enough to reach massive quasar hosts by redshift 6. Unlike many faint JWST sources, this system offers a direct, plausible path to early supermassive black holes.
arxiv-2602-12525:
The P3P problem asks for camera pose from three known points, but some camera spots, called singular cases, break the solution count. Xueying Sun led this work with two co-authors, using local dual space to give a complete geometric stratification of P3P singular cases by multiplicity mu of the camera centre O. The frame maps where singular cases sit.

For mu at least 2, O lies on the danger cylinder. For mu at least 3, O lies on one of three generatrices linked to the first Morley triangle or the circumcircle. For mu at least 4, O lies on the circumcircle itself. That case gives infinitely many P3P solutions. A complementary case O prime is also stratified. For mu at least 2, it lies on a deltoidal surface tied to the danger cylinder. For mu at least 3, it lies on one of three cuspidal curves of that surface.
arxiv-2602-12825:
Identifying an operating system from network traffic helps defenders, but standard classifiers give a single answer with no honest measure of doubt. Rubén Pérez-Jove and three co-authors bring conformal prediction to the task, wrapping existing methods to produce prediction sets with guaranteed coverage. A flat approach ignores the natural hierarchy of operating systems, so they test two structured variants that respect it.

Level-wise calibration treats each hierarchy level on its own, giving tight sets suited to human forensic work but allowing taxonomic inconsistencies. Projection-based calibration instead projects leaf sets upward, guaranteeing nested, consistent sets ideal for automated policy enforcement at some cost in efficiency. The paper maps that trade-off clearly, so users can pick the variant that fits their workflow.
arxiv-2602-13125:
Warm Jupiters on long orbits are prized for planet formation studies, but transiting examples remain scarce. Felipe Rojas and colleagues confirm TIC65910228b from a single TESS transit, measuring a mass of 4.554 Jupiter masses and radius 1.088 Jupiter radii on a roughly 180.52-day eccentric orbit around an evolved F-type star. Spectroscopic follow-up with FEROS and PLATOSpec supplied radial velocities, while photometry from HATPI and Observatoire Moana sharpened the period.

The planet joins a still thin population of long-period, massive transiting giants, one of few with mild eccentricity. Its discovery shows the power of single-transit events to populate an under-explored region of parameter space. The system also invites atmospheric and dynamical follow-up, helping test how giant planets form and migrate to wide, eccentric orbits.
arxiv-2602-13325:
Complex systems such as neural assemblies are hard to read from the inside, since activity traces hide wiring, cell types, and signal rules. This paper trains graph neural networks to predict observable activity in simulated assemblies of thousands of neurons, then uses the trained networks to pull the system apart into interpretable parts. The method jointly recovers the connectivity matrix, neuron types, signaling functions, and sometimes hidden external stimuli.

Unlike recurrent networks and transformers, which prize prediction over insight, this approach delivers both solid forecasts and a readable account of what drives the assembly. That pairing matters for science, where a forecast alone rarely explains a mechanism. Cedric Allier leads the work with three co-authors.
arxiv-2602-13425:
Nonlocal equations, where values at distant points influence a solution, behave differently from classical ones, and this paper studies nonnegative solutions of a sublinear nonlocal problem with fully nonlinear structure. The setting is a bounded convex domain with smooth boundary, driven by nonlocal Pucci extremal operators and a weight that may change sign. A new hypothesis on the negative part of the solution outside the domain plays a central role.

That hypothesis, together with the negative part of the potential, shapes whether dead cores form, regions where the solution vanishes, and it cannot be dropped. The proof leans on lower bounds for maxima of nontrivial solutions via Liouville theorems, plus a Hopf lemma for viscosity solutions that the authors also prove. Juan Pablo Cabeza leads the work with two co-authors.
arxiv-2602-13525:
Beams vibrate, and damping decides whether those vibrations die away gracefully or linger. This paper studies smoothness and decay for two coupled Euler-Bernoulli beam equations with localized singular damping, a concentrated damping setup that is mathematically delicate. Under suitable smoothness assumptions on the damping coefficient, the authors establish Gevrey smoothness for the solution family generated by the associated operator.

For a broader class of damping setups, including rougher damping, a uniform decay result is derived. Together the findings give a detailed account of long-term behavior for the coupled system, showing how that damping shapes decay and smoothness over time. K. Ammari leads the work with two co-authors.
arxiv-2602-14325:
Alon Danai and two co-authors generalize a 2026 arXiv result on two-dimensional subtraction-transfer games. These impartial, normal-play games use two piles of tokens, with players alternately taking tokens from a pile or transferring tokens between piles. Tamás Lengyel's earlier results and conjectures anchor the work.

The authors show that nim-values for a large class of such games are periodic, and in many cases they compute the exact period. Several new notions of periodicity are also developed, refining how periodic behavior is described. The results extend the theory of subtraction games into two dimensions, where transfer moves enrich the play.
arxiv-2602-14625:
Some orderings of a set keep crossings low, which helps search and geometry. Jan Dreier, with Clemens Kuske as co-author, gives a faster way to compute Welzl orders for set systems with linear neighborhood complexity. Earlier methods ran far slower on large inputs.

The new randomized method runs in near-linear expected time and reaches the best possible crossing bound. It also yields fast compact neighborhood covers for such graph classes. As a bonus, it cuts the cost of first-order model checking on monadically stable graphs. The result turns a theoretical ordering tool into a practical routine.
arxiv-2602-14825:
Kabir Chakravarti and Federico R. Urban study how binary formation channels shape the cross-correlation between gravitational wave events and galaxy catalogues. Five mock catalogues vary the progenitor-to-remnant mass-transfer function and the time-delay distribution, then cross-correlate against galaxy samples modelled on the 2MASS photometric redshift catalogue and the Gaia-unWISE quasar catalogue.

Uncertainty in formation channels leaves a mark on the predicted signal for current and next-generation detector networks, the authors find. So the correlation carries information about merger origins as well as large-scale structure. Gravitational waves plus galaxies become a joint probe of how binaries form. Formation history hides in the sky's cross-pattern.
arxiv-2602-14925:
Yuxi Lu and colleagues use the Magellanic Clouds to untangle extra mixing in the carbon-to-nitrogen age relation for metal-poor stars. The relation reconstructs Milky Way formation history from field giants, but below iron-to-hydrogen of minus 0.5, extra mixing alters surface carbon and nitrogen in mass- and metallicity-dependent ways that are poorly understood.

Within the Milky Way, old low-mass metal-poor stars entangle mass and metallicity, but the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds offer a wider laboratory for separating them. The paper explores that potential, testing how extra mixing behaves beyond the Galaxy. Stellar ages for metal-poor populations gain a clearer, if still challenging, calibration.
arxiv-2602-15125:
Chang and colleagues propose high-dimensional superdense coding with energy-time entangled states. It uses entanglement to boost classical communication capacity. It is a key quantum method. Their states are biphoton frequency combs, cases of grid states inspired by Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill codes. The method splits continuous time and frequency and encodes data through shifts in both.

That design taps the large Hilbert space of quantum combs while resisting timing and tuning errors. The team also sketches a lab build from standard telecom parts, fast single-photon detectors, and a splitter, and studies noise effects on the channel. With realistic settings, current tech works, reaching about 9 bits per transmitted photon, or 481 outcomes with tiny errors. That more than doubles the prior best of 4 bits and beats single-photon combs by more than fourfold.
arxiv-2602-15225:
Frongillo and colleagues propose position-optimization games, a general class of symmetric games. Given a probability distribution over targets, each player picks a position in a space. How well a player does depends on the share of targets for which that player is nearest, judged by some proximity measure, with ties shared evenly. Hotelling games and forecasting competitions are among the uses this model covers.

For player counts large enough, the team finds pure equilibria and symmetric mixed Nash equilibria, and both are extreme: every player chooses from a finite set of pseudo-targets. Both kinds of equilibria converge to the distribution induced by the target distribution, and the team bounds the convergence rate. The generality of the model extends and strengthens prior Hotelling work and proves new results for forecasting competitions and other applications.
arxiv-2602-15325:
Zhang and colleagues bridge farm base models and word models with an agent setup. Farm base models, taught on huge space-time data such as far scans, soil maps, and field notes, hit strong guesses and watching. These models lack word-based thinking and hands-on powers, cutting use in real jobs. Large word models shine at reading and writing text, but cannot straight think over high farm sets.

Their setup gives AgriWorld, a Python space with tools for map asks, far-scan stats, crop growth model, and guessers such as yield, stress, and sickness. On this space, they build Agro-Thinking, an LLM agent writing code, seeing outs, and tuning study via an execute-observe-refine loop. They offer AgroBench, with data making for farm QA across finds, guesses, oddity finding, and what-if tests. Tests beat text-only and direct rivals, proving run-driven review.
arxiv-2602-15425:
Zálešák and colleagues probe in theory the rise of dichroism in EELS for a model single-twist coil nano shape, giving a full study of the best settings to get a strong trace. The rise of round dichroism in twisted nanoscale and tiny systems gives a way for reading the bit twist itself. It adds extra levels of room in steering light. Such steering can be hit even at the nanoscale level; however, sensing and grasping light zones well below the spread edge needs a fitting tool.

EELS with spin-based e-state sifting has been floated as an apt hopeful, but to date, no final tests have been done. Their work gives new ideas into the reading and swing of the spin-resolved EELS trace, which can spark and steer later lab work.
arxiv-2602-15525:
Bogaty and Tuzhilin recast a classic result, the Mazur-Ulam theorem, in the language of Gromov-Hausdorff distance. They show that two Banach spaces are linearly isometric exactly when the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between them is finite, and in particular zero. The proof gathers results from many hands on how near-surjective near-isometries can be approximated by true linear surjective isometries.

For finite-dimensional spaces, the authors give a simpler proof under weaker assumptions than an earlier one by Mikhailov, plus a criterion for isometry stated through finite compact subsets. The paper is short on new machinery and long on synthesis, tying scattered approximation results into one clean characterisation. Readers of metric geometry will find a handy bridge between distance and linear structure.
arxiv-2602-15725:
Working alone, Chaudhry targets a weakness of large language models: on benchmarks that demand compositional reasoning, ARC-AGI-2 and GPQA, plus MATH, BBH, and HLE, accuracy collapses, despite strong showings elsewhere. Current remedies widen search at the token level, using prompted step-by-step reasoning, votes across samples, or learning from rewards, yet the model's hidden representation space stays put. When a needed abstraction is not already encoded there, performance falls apart.

His Recursive Concept Evolution frame lets pretrained models reshape their internal representation geometry during inference. Low-rank concept subspaces are spawned when representational inadequacy is detected, merged when synergistic, picked by a minimum description length criterion, and consolidated by constrained optimisation to preserve stability. With Mistral-7B, the method gains 12 to 18 points on ARC-AGI-2, 8 to 14 points on GPQA and BBH, and reduces depth-induced error on MATH and HLE.
arxiv-2602-15925:
Mensch and colleagues built Stochastic Gradient Lattice Random Walk, or SGLRW, for robust stochastic gradient posterior sampling. Stochastic-gradient MCMC methods scale Bayesian posterior sampling well, but they often react badly to minibatch size and gradient noise. SGLRW extends lattice random walk discretisation.

Unlike standard stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics, SGLRW adds stochastic noise only through off-diagonal parts of the update covariance. That yields stronger robustness to minibatch size while keeping asymptotic correctness. As a check, the authors also study a natural SGLD analogue using gradient clipping. Tests on Bayesian regression and classification show SGLRW holding steady where SGLD fails, even under heavy-tailed gradient noise, and matching or beating predictive scores.
arxiv-2602-16125:
Leo Muxing Wang leads a team of three researchers who ask which data sources should train a shared feature extractor. Joint training over all related sources is standard practice. Sources with low relevance or poor quality hurt representation learning. The paper digs into a subtler case: one where each source looks good, with similar relevance and quality relative to the true common structure. It asks whether screening still helps there.

In the linear setting, where sources share a low-dimensional subspace, the answer is yes. Screening plays a central role in statistically optimal subspace estimation. For a broad class of problems, training on a hand-picked subset suffices for minimax optimality, even when much data is set aside. The authors define an informative subpopulation and build tools to find such subsets, tested on synthetic and real data. The lesson: more sources do not always mean better representations.
arxiv-2602-16325:
Xiaoyu Zhang, writing alone, develops a unified way to evaluate the squared total spin of excited states in two-component time-dependent density functional theory. That theory already covers noncollinear excitations in noncollinear starting states, plus spin-conserving and spin-flip excitations in collinear ones. The paper sets out a general formalism for the expectation value of the squared total spin within that setting.

Zhang then derives specialized forms for collinear cases, where the theory splits into conventional spin-conserving and spin-flip theory. The working forms are compared in detail with earlier theoretical approaches. The analysis shows the excited-state value comes from two distinct sources: the starting state's own value, plus an extra part added when the state is excited. Calculations based on the same theory, unrestricted Kohn-Sham, and restricted open-shell Kohn-Sham starting states put the method to work.
arxiv-2602-16425:
Somnath Majumder and Krishnendu Mukherjee study fermion mass generation in a scalar-fermion quartic theory. The calculation uses the Cornwall, Jackiw and Tomboulis method, summing infinite two-particle irreducible diagrams of two types plus a diagram of a third type. The effective potential is symmetric under sign flips of the field.

Beyond an open set of positive real numbers, the potential has maxima and minima above and below the zero line. Those extremes sit either side of the minimum at zero field value. In that region the fermion acquires mass when the system settles at a positive, nonzero field value, breaking inversion symmetry of the vacuum. When the coupling constant falls inside that open set, the potential has its minimum only at zero field value, and the fermion stays massless. The paper maps where mass generation switches on and off with the coupling.
arxiv-2602-16525:
Shafagh Abband Pashaki, Sepehr Maleki, and Amir Badiee propose a way to keep home power grids within safe limits. Households get paid to shift or cut use at peak times. A service provider sets hourly incentive rates from wholesale prices and total home load. Home energy systems weigh appliance needs and the cost of annoyance. Both provider and user money interests enter the design.

A deep reinforcement learning method learns the best rates in real time under firm capacity limits. Tests used real use and price data from three households. Peak demand fell and the total load curve grew smoother. The peak-to-average ratio dropped by a large margin against no demand response. Grid planners get a tested scheme that eases congestion without ignoring what households want.
arxiv-2602-16825:
Ahmad Ahmad, Shuo Liu, Roberto Tron, and Calin Belta present RRT-eta, a sampling-based motion planning and control frame from Signal Temporal Logic specs using arithmetic-geometric mean robustness. Sampling-based planning probes knotty, high-dimensional config spaces, and Signal Temporal Logic states readable robot tasks with space-time constraints. Old routes use min-max robustness, which looks only at key times and subformulae, making jagged optimization lands that hinder tree search.

RRT-eta instead uses arithmetic-geometric mean robustness, judging fit across all times and subformulae. Gains include interval semantics for partial paths during tree building, a fast incremental monitoring code, and enhanced satisfaction-direction vectors using fulfillment priority logic. The frame builds dynamically feasible controls meeting logic specs with high robustness while keeping probabilistic completeness.
arxiv-2602-16925:
Brandon Schweers and M. Virginia McSwain run stellar paternity tests, matching high-latitude B stars to the open clusters of their birth. OB stars generally form in open clusters within the Milky Way's thin disk. High-latitude finds are thought to have been ejected from birth clusters during the past few tens of millions of years. Using Gaia Data Release 3, the authors traced paths of thirty-nine high-latitude B-type stars and hundreds of Galactic open clusters, hunting past intersections.

Where paths matched, cluster HR diagrams were checked to confirm parent-orphan pairs share matching ages. Further study of cluster cores helped determine a probable ejection mechanism. Possible origins were identified for five orphaned B-type stars. Likely travel times, ejection velocities, and runaway mechanisms are discussed. One star whose path never neared the disk in the study period is also discussed, with possible origins weighed.
arxiv-2602-17125:
Mao-Jun Yan, writing alone, decodes two exotic particle states that sit near an important threshold. The states in question, members of the X(4140) family and the X1(4685), resist simple classification. The paper studies OZI-suppressed coupled-channel scattering in B decays to D_s D_s K, using the effective range expansion. The X0(4140), tied to a dip in the observed lineshape, emerges as a dynamically generated pole near the J/psi phi threshold.

Treating spin-spin forces as a secondary effect, the author predicts a virtual state with matching quantum numbers near the same threshold, resolving puzzles about the X1(4140) width. Heavy quark spin symmetry then lets the X1(4685) be read as a psi(2S) phi hadronic molecule. Together the results show these states as windows into Fierz rearrangement and OZI suppression in low-energy strong interactions.
arxiv-2602-17625:
Obaidullah Zaland and team tackle federated learning under two strains at once: scarce communication and data that arrives in stages. Standard federated learning assumes a fixed data flow and many rounds, so staged tasks and forgetting pose real trouble. Their system, OSI-FL, is billed as the first to face both strains together.

Each client sends category-specific embeddings, built by a frozen vision-language model, in a single round. A pretrained diffusion model at the server then makes new samples like the client's data, and training runs on those samples. Selective Sample Retention keeps the most telling samples per category and task, bounding forgetting as new tasks land. Tests beat baselines in both class-incremental and domain-incremental settings on three benchmarks.
arxiv-2602-17725:
Jericho Cain studies whether ambient phase shifts in gravitational-wave signals can be seen with no matched templates. Effects such as triple motion impose total phase shifts through shifting line-of-sight acceleration. Whether such smooth time-warp warps show up depends jointly on deformation strength and signal-to-noise ratio, a link not yet measured in a template-free frame.

Using time-frequency views from the ongoing wavelet transform, Cain analyzes path-level stats, above all the power-weighted frequency centroid. Ambient shifts prove visible with a single-sample stat tied to an isolated-binary spread. Across a grid of warps and signal strengths, scores collapse onto a single scaling number: total phase shift times signal-to-noise ratio. Mid-size warps show even at low signal strength, while small ones need higher strength.
arxiv-2602-17925:
Neda Barbazi and team study how children with chronic conditions manage daily life, peer ties and clinical care across ages. Younger children lean on parental support, while older ones seek independence. Prior work used proxy-based, family-centered and playful approaches, yet most tools treat children as one uniform group rather than adapting to age differences.

The team ran four co-design workshops with sixty-nine children with congenital heart disease at a medically supported camp, spanning elementary, middle and high school groups. Younger children relied on comfort objects and reassurance, middle schoolers used aided communication and selective sharing, and high schoolers stressed agency and direct talks with peers and providers. The study offers observed lessons for pediatric tools that adapt across age paths, grounded in child-centered hands-on design.
arxiv-2602-18325:
Sylwia Antoniuk and three co-authors study how cheaply a buyer can build small target graphs in a random edge stream. Their 2026 paper treats the budget-constrained random graph process, where each offered edge must be bought or passed forever, with a deadline and a cap on purchases. The goal is a graph holding a chosen small subgraph.

For the complete graph on four vertices, the team proves an optimal strategy and a matching budget threshold: above it, success is nearly certain; below it, no strategy can succeed. That settles a question posed by Iľkovič, León, and Shu. Tight results follow for wheels of any fixed size and for a tree plus one universal vertex, while the five-vertex complete graph gets upper and lower bounds with a gap still open.
arxiv-2602-18425:
Deniz Qian and two co-authors built RVR, a multi-round retrieval framework for questions with many valid answers. Their 2026 paper notes comprehensively retrieving diverse documents is crucial when a query admits a wide range of correct answers. RVR starts with a retriever returning candidate documents, then a verifier picks a high-quality subset.

Later rounds augment the query with previously verified documents to uncover answers not yet covered. The method works even with ready-made retrievers, and fine-tuning retrievers for this inference procedure adds further gains. It beats baselines including agentic search, gaining at least ten percent relative and three percent absolute in complete recall on the QAMPARI multi-answer dataset. Gains hold on QUEST and WebQuestionsSP across base retrievers. The work offers a promising iterative route to comprehensive answer recall.
arxiv-2602-18625:
William A. Gardner and one co-author trace shared solar irregularity. Their 2026 paper notes recently discovered time phases in Sunspot records, the approximate twenty-seven-day plasma rotation and eleven-year pole reversal share a common irregularity pattern. Since measurement holds an unknown constant delay of no practical import, average delay is subtracted out.

The remaining cycle goes zero to maximum delay, back to zero, then to maximum advance, and back to zero. The period of this cycle is estimated at one hundred sixty-four years, allowing no full repetition in the two hundred five-year record, so it may or may not continue. Nevertheless, shared irregularity across two long-recognized periodicities tied to distinct phenomena suggests one common phenomenon. A physics-based link between interior rotation speed and surface rotation period suggests one phenomenon may drive irregularity in both interior rotation and the pole-reversal period.
arxiv-2602-18825:
Ordinary neural networks can be pruned to sparse subnetworks that train just as well. That is the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis. Nicholas Kuhn, with five co-authors, asks in 2026 whether the same holds for Bayesian neural networks. Those networks quantify uncertainty, but they cost far more compute than standard ones.

The authors translate classic lottery ticket tests into a Bayesian setting, using usual computer vision models. They find winning tickets do exist, with matching or better accuracy, across model sizes. Accuracy degrades only at very high sparsity. Pruning should lean first on magnitude, then on standard deviation. Models also rely on mask structure and weight starting points to varying degrees.
arxiv-2602-19025:
Mixture-of-experts models combine several graph views through a learned router, but explaining their decisions is hard. Hossein Shokouhinejad, with three co-authors, investigates routing-aware explanations in 2026 for mixture-of-experts models for malware detection, using control flow graphs.

Diversity is built at two levels. At node level, each layer computes several neighbourhood statistics. A multilayer perceptron fuses them, guided by a degree reweighting factor. Pooling uses mean, standard deviation, or maximum. At readout level, six experts produce graph-level logits. Each expert covers one view. The router weights those logits into a prediction. For explanation, edge-level attributions are computed per expert and weighted by router gates. The rationale then shows each expert's focus and its selection strength. Against single-expert baselines, the mixture model achieves detection accuracy with stable, faithful attributions.
arxiv-2602-19125:
Neutron-star crusts may contain nuclear pasta, exotic shapes of dense matter. Vishal Parmar, with one co-author, quantifies that pasta in 2026 with a Bayesian ensemble of unified equations of state. Relativistic mean-field models anchor the ensemble. Nuclear experiments, saturation properties, chiral theory, and multimessenger data constrain it.

Pasta onset, thickness, and mass fraction are computed for each posterior sample. The symmetry-energy slope mainly controls pasta appearance and extent. Spherical and rod shapes appear in every equation of state. Slab, tube, and bubble shapes appear only rarely. The sphere-to-rod transition density is tightly constrained. Pasta occupies a modest radial thickness but a large mass fraction. Crustal oscillation frequencies follow, correlating strongly with symmetry-energy curvature at sub-saturation density. Observed low-frequency oscillations thus constrain crust physics.
arxiv-2602-19225:
Language-model agents now handle multi-step jobs in customer service, shopping help, and task management, where training must separate real skill from random luck. A failure on an easy task may mean only noise, while success on a hard one may mark a genuine breakthrough. Yet common training methods score whole batches by simple statistics, so they often credit the wrong steps when task difficulty swings.

Yangyi Fang and six colleagues offer a proximity-based fix for this credit problem. Instead of judging each turn only against its batch mates, it weighs how close a turn sits to the outcome it helped produce. Steps near a success earn more credit, and steps far from it earn less, even when difficulty varies across the batch. The goal is faster, steadier training for agents that must act over many turns.
arxiv-2602-19525:
A stain on the wall gets covered with non-overlapping stickers of one identical shape, allowing rotation and reflection. Keigo Oka and two co-authors ask whether some sticker shape must fail to cover the stain, studying the problem under polyomino constraints. They finish the classification of always-coverable stain shapes, proving which maximal polyominoes are always coverable.

Concrete counterexamples show minimal not always-coverable cases exist, even among hole-free polyominoes. The classification yields an algorithm to decide always-coverability for any given stain. Determining whether one sticker can cover one stain is NP-complete, though exact cover is not demanded. The result extends to the one-dimensional case without connectivity.
arxiv-2602-19725:
A swinging mass loses energy through friction, but friction comes in several forms: steady resistance, resistance proportional to speed, and resistance proportional to speed squared. A 2026 arXiv paper by Robert Pezer and Karlo Lelas derives simple approximate formulas for energy loss under all three, named Coulomb, Stokes, and Newton damping.

The method builds on the free oscillator and on the link between energy loss rates and the power spent by damping forces. It gives a direct account of energy without first solving for amplitude. The formulas prove remarkably accurate against exact and computational checks. The authors also derive an exact solution for Stokes damping by a fresh route, and pitch the whole treatment at a level suited to undergraduate or advanced school physics teaching.
arxiv-2602-19925:
Mixtures of bosons and fermions can form self-bound quantum droplets, but most theory treats them at zero temperature. A 2026 arXiv paper by Maciej Lewkowicz and three co-authors uses numerical methods to study three-dimensional Bose-Fermi droplets at nonzero temperatures.

The team models an attractive atomic mixture two ways: with quantum hydrodynamics plus corrections beyond mean-field theory and heat effects, and with a simplified Hartree-Fock model. They find cold droplets that last a finite time can hold together in free space when attraction between bosons and fermions is strong enough. Droplets can also sit in a box trap in balance with surrounding boson and fermion vapour. Droplet traits are traced to starting condensate share, total atom count, and how strongly the species attract.
arxiv-2602-20025:
Partition theory studies sums over parts of partitions, and two functions introduced by Andrews and Ghosh Dastidar count odd parts minus even parts, with and without distinctness. A 2026 arXiv paper by Nayandeep Deka Baruah and Pankaj Gogoi studies the arithmetic of the distinct-parts version, called DSOME.

Andrews and Ghosh Dastidar had expressed generating functions for both functions as q-series and found congruences modulo four and five. The new paper writes the generating function of DSOME in closed form. From that form the authors derive new congruences and internal congruences modulo four and eight for DSOME. Readers gain a closed-form handle on DSOME and a fresh set of divisibility patterns for its values.
arxiv-2602-20425:
Sol LeWitt famously counted all incomplete open cubes, finding one hundred twenty-two connected, non-planar subsets of the cube's edges. Mikael Vejdemo-Johansson extends that enumeration to the other Platonic solids, counting incomplete open versions of each. An incomplete open solid keeps only some edges of the solid, connected and non-planar.

The counts are six tetrahedra, one hundred twenty-two cubes matching LeWitt, one hundred eighty-five octahedra, more than two point four million dodecahedra, and more than sixteen million icosahedra. No enumeration had been published for any other solid before this work. The paper thus completes the Platonic family that LeWitt began with the cube.
arxiv-2602-20925:
Thermal cameras help robots see in bad light and weather, but thermal mapping at large scale stays difficult. Zeyu Jiang, Kuan Xu, and Changhao Chen present LST-SLAM in this 2026 arXiv paper, a stereo thermal system built for kilometer-scale dynamic outdoor scenes. It combines self-supervised thermal feature learning with stereo motion tracking at two levels and geometric pose optimization.

A semantic-geometric constraint suppresses moving features that lack consistent geometry between frames, while an online bag-of-words model finds loop closures and global optimization removes drift. Tests on large dynamic thermal datasets show the system beating recent rivals, including AirSLAM and DROID-SLAM, in robustness and accuracy. Robots get a mapping stack that survives the conditions where ordinary cameras fail.
arxiv-2602-21025:
The LSZ argument links scattering amplitudes in flat space to correlation functions of field operators, but its details confuse many readers. S. P. de Alwis reviews the original argument in this 2026 arXiv paper and clarifies the confusing issues. The notes then take up the origin of the i-epsilon prescriptions, following Weinberg, without assuming the vacuum is free at asymptotic times.

The same circle of ideas is then carried into inflationary cosmology, where the author stresses that unitarity-violating contour deformations are unnecessary. Readers get a careful walk through prescriptions that are often applied by rote, in both flat space and cosmological settings. The emphasis throughout is on what each step actually assumes.
arxiv-2602-21325:
High-energy partons lose energy crossing the hot medium of nucleus-nucleus collisions, suppressing high-momentum particle production. The CMS Collaboration studies how that suppression depends on system size in this 2026 arXiv letter, across four collision systems at the CERN Large Hadron Collider. Previous oxygen, xenon, and lead measurements are recast on identical momentum intervals.

They are joined by the first neon-neon charged-particle measurement at five point three six teraelectronvolts. Suppression trends look similar across systems but scale with nucleon number, with a downward slope at low momentum, a local minimum around five to seven gigaelectronvolts, and a rise thereafter. Initial-state-only models fail, while energy-loss models succeed above about ten gigaelectronvolts.
arxiv-2602-21425:
Abel Gonçalves Chinaglia and two co-authors present tugturn, a Python workflow for markerless three-dimensional analysis of the Timed Up and Go test. Instrumented TUG analysis can aid clinical and research decisions. But robust, reproducible markerless pipelines have stayed scarce.

The pipeline splits each trial into stand, first gait, turning, second gait, and sit phases using spatial thresholds. It detects heel-strike and toe-off events by a relative-distance rule inside valid gait windows. Beyond standard kinematics, it adds Vector Coding outputs and extrapolated-center-of-mass stability metrics. Settings live in TOML files, and outputs include HTML reports, CSV tables, and quality-assurance visuals, with a runnable example and test data included.
arxiv-2602-21825:
Steering light-matter links is central to light tools, from lasers to optical information processing. Well-designed light setups give flat bands, where the density of states spikes and group speed drops to zero, letting light sit still. These traits make flat bands good for lasing, yet building such setups is hard. Rebecca Heilmann and four co-authors introduce nano chain grids.

These chain shapes provide long-range coupled systems holding flat bands over the angular range. The team shows transverse-mode lasing in single nano chains and the shift from flat band lasing to single-mode head-on lasing as chains grow. They also show partly synced glow from square and three-sided flat chain lattices, with modes set by pump power and spin. Chain grids offer a handy platform for flat band lasing and new routes toward narrow, straight aligned, bright sources.
arxiv-2602-21925:
Chi Hin Chan, Jun-Shuo Chen, and Cheng-Fang Su solve a classic equation of vector calculus on ring-shaped regions in any dimension from two up. The task is to find a smooth vector field whose divergence matches a given source term, where the source is smooth and its total over the region is zero. Their 2026 arXiv paper builds the answer with a fresh method drawn from differential topology.

The method departs from the two standard approaches and leans on a clever topological argument, which reduces the hard step to a problem in linear algebra. The resulting field is smooth, matches the source exactly, and drops to zero on both edges of the ring. Readers get a new route to explicit solutions, plus a worked link to a well-known fact about the cohomology of Euclidean space.
arxiv-2602-22125:
Instruction-following tests are mostly English, leaving hundreds of millions of Indic-language speakers without a fair yardstick. Thanmay Jayakumar and four co-authors introduce IndicIFEval, a benchmark for constrained generation across fourteen Indic languages, using instructions that can be checked by rule. Each language gets hundreds of human-verified examples, split between localized translations and newly written native content.

Evaluations of major open and proprietary models show a split: formatting rules are mostly obeyed, while lexical and cross-lingual tasks trip models up badly. Progress in high-resource languages has not closed the gap for the wider Indic family. The benchmark gives builders a concrete target for serving India's languages as well as they serve English.
arxiv-2602-22425:
Designing computer chips is slow, skilled work, and demand for compute keeps exploding. Raghav Gupta and twelve co-authors present ArchAgent, an agentic AI system for automated computer-architecture discovery built on AlphaEvolve. It designs and implements new mechanisms, not just tunes parameters, within an established cache-replacement design competition.

In two days without human help, ArchAgent produced a cache policy beating the prior best by about five percent on multi-core workload traces. On heavily explored single-core workloads, it needed eighteen days to gain under one percent over the existing best. The system shows agentic AI can discover real hardware mechanisms, even where human exploration has been intense.
arxiv-2602-22525:
Zhonghao Zhan and three co-authors test the security of language-model agents run on small home devices rather than in the cloud. They built a home-automation testbed with local MQTT messaging and an Android phone as an edge inference node. Against it they compare cloud-hosted, edge-local swarm, and hybrid setups. They find five systems-level attack surfaces, including two failures seen live: coordination-state divergence and induced trust erosion.

Edge-local setups end routine cloud data exposure, but fallback steps quietly cross sovereignty boundaries in ways the app layer cannot see. Provenance chains hold while devices cooperate yet break easily without cryptographic enforcement, and failover windows open brief blind spots an attacker could use for unauthorized control. The lesson is that deployment shape, not just model or prompt design, drives risk.
arxiv-2602-22925:
Katerina Papagiannouli and two co-authors push Bayesian neural networks past Gaussian-process limits. Wide Bayesian networks gather after-data beliefs through rare but leading swings, and large-gap theory supplies plain varying goals, rate functions, on guessers, giving a function notion of hardness and feature learning.

The after-data output rate function comes from joint tuning over guessers and internal kernels, unlike fixed-kernel NNGP theory. Test experiments show the ensuing guesses describe finite-width conduct well for fairly sized networks, catching non-Gaussian tails, after-data warping, and data-tied kernel choice. For theorists, the work moves feature learning from kernel folklore to function-level varying principle.
arxiv-2602-23225:
Pengxiang Li and four co-authors ask why diffusion language models, sold as at-once generators, so often fall back into left-to-right, step-by-step decoding. Genuine at-once generation could remove the sequential bottleneck, exploit parallel hardware better, and improve latency as outputs grow. Yet practical fast diffusion models keep sliding into sequential habits.

The authors blame a mismatch between diffusion goals and the highly sequential training data, including standard early-training text and long thought-chain guidance. Their proof-of-concept fix, NAP, curates cases as multiple stand-alone thought paths and pairs them with a parallel-forced decoding plan that favors multi-token updates. On math benchmarks, NAP beats models trained on long thought-chain data under parallel decoding, with gains that grow as more work runs at once.
arxiv-2602-23325:
Francesco Di Braccio and four co-authors prove that every n-vertex 4-uniform hypergraph with minimum codegree at least n over 4, rounded down, contains a spanning tight component. A hypergraph generalizes a graph by letting edges join more than two vertices, and a tight component is a maximal tightly connected piece. The minimum codegree condition says every triple of vertices shares many common neighbors.

The bound is tight, meaning it cannot be lowered in general, and the result settles the 4-uniform case of a conjecture by Illingworth, Lang, Müyesser, Parczyk, and Sgueglia. For researchers in extremal combinatorics, the theorem closes a case that had resisted proof and sharpens the picture of when large hypergraphs are forced to hang together tightly.
arxiv-2602-23525:
Steven G. Johnson and one co-author review the engineering of fast Fourier transforms in practice. First published in 2008 as a chapter in a book on fast Fourier transforms, the review explains why optimized FFTs differ sharply from textbook radix-2 Cooley-Tukey algorithms.

The gap comes from hardware: optimized codes compensate for the memory hierarchy and exploit large register sets and deep pipelines of modern CPUs. Using the FFTW library as a case study, the authors discuss tradeoffs in recursion, generation of twiddle factors, code generation, and other algorithmic choices. The result is a high-level guide to what makes high-performance FFT implementations fast in the real world, beyond the abstract algorithm.
arxiv-2602-23825:
Nicholas Connolly and two co-authors study equivalence classes of graphs under local complementation, an operation that flips edges inside the neighborhood of a chosen vertex. The 2026 paper tackles the size of those classes for distance-hereditary graphs, a broad family where earlier formulas covered only paths and cycles.

The approach uses split decomposition, which breaks a graph into simpler prime pieces, to set upper bounds on class sizes. The authors then prove those bounds tight by counting the decomposed structures up to symmetry. Explicit formulas follow for several families, including complete multipartite graphs, clique-stars, and repeater graphs. The work extends a hard counting problem beyond tiny brute-force cases and gives exact class sizes for a wide, structured family.
arxiv-2602-24125:
Rohit Chivukula and three co-authors compare recommendation algorithms in the movie domain, treating recommendation as a regression task. The 2026 paper uses the Netflix challenge dataset, exploring user rating behavior and movie characteristics before extracting varied features.

Models tested include an XGBoost regression algorithm plus nearest-neighbor and matrix factorization methods from a standard recommendation library. Judged by root mean square error, matrix factorization approaches give the best recommendations. The study illustrates how feature engineering and model choice interact in movie recommendation. It offers a practical comparison for builders of streaming recommenders. In short, the best model wins on a simple error score. The score is easy to read and hard to game. That score is root mean square error. The team reports it for all models.
arxiv-2602-24225:
Adeel Mahmood studies weighted unequal error protection over a Rayleigh fading channel, where a message is split into blocks and the goal weights each block's decoding success probability. The 2026 solo paper models quasi-static Rayleigh fading with channel state information at the receiver but not at the transmitter, a realistic asymmetry for wireless links.

The author analyzes asymptotic and finite-blocklength performance for two achievability schemes: power-domain superposition, which layers blocks in power, and orthogonal resource allocation, also known as time-sharing, which splits time or bandwidth. Upper bounds on the optimal number of blocks are derived, with algorithms for optimal and locally optimal power and time splits. Results show superposition beating time-sharing, but by under two percent in both regimes, and they bound the gap between asymptotic and finite-blocklength performance, which shrinks as blocklength grows. The comparison guides designers choosing between layered and shared protection schemes.
arxiv-2603-00025: Fodeh's team tackles preference tuning for ontology-driven structured prediction, where chosen and turned-down JSON outputs differ by only a few schema-key tokens. Plain sequence-level DPO spreads learning signal over side tokens and can erode rare chosen tokens, so they build barely changed, schema-valid bad examples from expert ambiguity patterns and schema-error modes. Their TAB-PO method adds a confidence-gated token-level barrier that holds unsure schema tokens. It lifts ontology-critical scores well above supervised fine-tuning and strong DPO rivals.
arxiv-2603-00125: Rinne, Nikulin and Mäkelä extend the classical KKT framework to optimisation with generalised invex fuzzy functions, where goals and constraints are nonsmooth, vector-valued and fuzzy-valued. They derive fresh KKT-type conditions under weaker-than-classical convexity assumptions, giving weak Pareto optimality in fuzzy settings without needing differentiability or convexity. Their results tie together earlier work by Antczak and Mishra, and show the power of generalised invexity for optimality. Several worked cases show the theory's uses.
arxiv-2603-00525: Chan, Dexter, and Begelman run three dimensional simulations of black hole accretion that include electron positron pair physics, tracking pairs as a constant temperature scalar. At high accretion rates the pair fraction peaks near one percent, as inferred from some X-ray binaries, with a pair void near the hole. Pairs peak outside the plunging region and at the corona base, near equilibrium where scattering is thick. In the upper corona and jets, pairs exceed equilibrium by orders of magnitude, carried mainly by advection from the disk.
arxiv-2603-00625: Kashif, Marchisio, and Shafique close the cost estimation loop for hybrid quantum classical neural networks, where flop counts and gate counts miss gate durations, connectivity limits, and noise. Their analytical quantum cost model prices hardware resources from real backend calibration data, including durations, routing overheads, and noise driven sampling waste. A classical cost model converts flops into device specific throughput, giving one time based cost language for both halves. The paired models guide resource aware neural architecture search for hybrid networks.
arxiv-2603-00825: Agarwal and seven colleagues build COMBAT, a real time action controlled world model trained on Tekken 3, simulating a dynamic reactive foe. A 1.2 billion parameter Diffusion Transformer, fed by deep autoencoder latents, uses causal distillation and diffusion forcing for real time inference. Skilled foe behaviour emerges from training solely on single player inputs, with no explicit supervision of the foe's policy. Unlike imitation learning, which needs complete action labels, COMBAT learns quick behaviour from partial data.
arxiv-2603-00925: Lucy and four colleagues benchmark eleven vision-language models on DrawEduMath, a year-long collection of real students' handwritten math work. Every model fares worse on work from students needing the most teaching help, and error-assessment questions prove hardest across the board. The findings suggest models tuned as math solvers still need different incentives before they can genuinely support classroom teaching.
arxiv-2603-01425: Jin and six colleagues describe LaSER, a 2026 framework that moves reasoning into a dense retriever's latent space, so it reasons silently instead of writing its reasoning out before searching. It trains one shared backbone with two views. One encodes known reasoning paths openly, the other thinks in hidden states, and an alignment step keeps the hidden path matched to the open stages. On reasoning-heavy tests inside and outside its training domain, LaSER beat the best existing baselines while keeping a standard retriever's speed.
arxiv-2603-01525:
Haoxuan Xie and Siqiang Luo tackle search in vector databases when each item also carries a sequence, such as text or DNA. Their 2026 work adds pattern rules, like the database commands that check if a string contains a given piece. Old tools filter by plain traits or ranges, but not by such patterns inside sequences.

Their index, VectorMaton, merges pattern checks with nearest-vector search in one enhanced automaton structure. The index stays close in size to the raw data set, which keeps storage costs sane. Tests on real data sets show far higher query speed than rival tools at the same accuracy. Index size also drops sharply in the tests. The work brings a classic database skill to modern AI search stacks.
arxiv-2603-01625:
Aditya Parikh, Aasa Feragen, Sneha Das, and Stella Frank warn that good test scores can hide weak radiology reports. Their 2026 work studies AI models that turn X-ray images into written reports. Some decoding choices yield safe, generic text that scores well on word overlap yet drops key clinical terms.

They call that failure template collapse, since reports shrink to a few stock phrases. To expose it, they track how word links tied to patient groups shift between real and made reports. A weighted score sums that loss of clinical signal across groups. Fixed decoding erases the most signal, while random sampling adds variety but can add new bias. The authors urge diversity checks as a core part of judging report models.
arxiv-2603-01925:
Maxwell Piper and Alison Crocker double the known sample of counter-rotating disk galaxies in a major survey. Their 2026 work studies galaxies with two stellar disks that spin in opposite directions in one plane. Such systems offer a rare window on gas accretion and on how galaxies assemble over time.

Past visual hunts in the MaNGA survey found only a few dozen confirmed cases. The pair train an automated pre-selection method on those cases to weed out unlikely hosts. Applied to a newer data release, the method yields many new confirmed systems plus a larger candidate list. Emission-line diagrams of the new sample match a control set of early-type galaxies closely. That null result says line diagnostics alone cannot flag counter-rotating disks or set them apart today.
arxiv-2603-02025:
Yue Niu, Zhaokai Sun, Jiayi Yang, and colleagues open the black box of graph neural networks with a concept layer. Their 2026 work asks how such networks turn graph patterns into logical rules behind each prediction. Past explainers recover only hard rules and run after training, so they may misstate the true reasoning.

Their layer, built into any graph network, forces predictions through selected global graph concepts first. Concept scores then pass through a sparse linear layer to reach the class label. That path enforces soft logical rules and lets each concept contribution be quantified per prediction. Language models embed the concepts by treating concepts as graph words and graphs as graph sentences. Tests show top marks for both classification accuracy and interpretability.
arxiv-2603-02725:
Xiaodong Li, Juwei Yue, Xinghua Zhang, and colleagues help new users of one service by borrowing taste signals from another. Their 2026 model, S2CDR, addresses cross-domain recommendation for cold-start users with no local history. Diffusion-based rivals transfer preferences well but ignore links between items across domains, and their added noise can blur personal taste.

The new design replaces noise with a two-way flow. A smoothing step spreads interaction data across an item-similarity graph using a heat-style rule and a filter that keeps the clean signal. A sharpening step then rebuilds the missing interactions for new users, guided by differential equations. Across three real test cases, the training-free method beat the best prior systems.
arxiv-2603-03325:
Guanming Liu and ten colleagues build a proxy agent that learns what a particular user really wants. Inferring intent from context is hard, because it takes both the immediate situation and the motives behind behavior. Most systems treat the job as one-off recognition and ignore the patterns a user has built up over time. Their 2026 system, IntPro, remembers those patterns on purpose.

IntPro stores short explanations of how past context signals led to past intents in a personal history library, then retrieves relevant ones when a new case arrives. Training mixes supervised fine-tuning with multi-turn reinforcement learning that rewards wise use of the history. Across three varied scenarios, from post syncing to intent datasets, IntPro understood intent strongly and reasoned about context well across different base models.
arxiv-2603-03725:
Yifan Zhu and three others explain why poisoned training data can make a data set unlearnable, using information theory. Unlearnable cases carry invisible tweaks that stop unauthorized models from generalizing, protecting data owners. Current recipes were built on hunches. Their 2026 paper shows the common thread: effective poisons always shrink the mutual information between clean features and poisoned features, and deeper networks squeeze it further as protection improves.

A proof from covariance shape follows: shrinking the conditional covariance within each class lowers that mutual information. Their method, MI-UE, therefore maximizes the cosine similarity among same-class poisoned features, collapsing the covariance directly. Extensive tests show it beating earlier unlearnable example methods sharply, and holding up even when the learner deploys known defense mechanisms against the poisoning.
arxiv-2603-03825:
Ruilin Luo and others study the cold-start initialization stage of multimodal large reasoning models, the phase that prepares such models for reinforcement learning. They introduce the Visual Attention Score, a metric that measures how much a model attends to visual tokens, and find that reasoning results is tightly linked to it. Surprisingly, a multimodal cold-start does not raise this score, a failure the authors call Lazy Attention Localization, while a text-only cold-start does.

Training-free interventions that shift attention during inference improve results, confirming the effect is causal. Building on this, the authors propose the AVAR framework, which combines visual-anchored data synthesis, attention-guided objectives, and visual-anchored rewards. It gains notably across seven multimodal reasoning benchmarks on the model tested, and ablations credit each component.
arxiv-2603-03925: Christopher Popp and others present a unified stabilizer-based resource distillation method for prime-dimension quantum systems. By treating stabilizer routines as quantum channels and working out output forms, the method applies stabilizer steps to general inputs and diverse objectives. Several plans are presented for fidelity tuning and for optimizing coherent and private information in both regimes.
arxiv-2603-04025: Nikjoo and others report weak lensing by photometric density ridges in Dark Energy Survey Year 3 data. Ridges in galaxy density fields from photometric surveys are two-dimensional projections of cosmic-web filaments, so they should lens light from background galaxies. The team detects this effect with strong significance, though intertwined with galaxy-galaxy lensing, and aids the subspace-constrained mean shift method to locate ridges efficiently at scale. Simulations show the signal depends primarily on the S8 cosmological setting, and the authors discuss methodology gains needed for sharpness setting gauging.
arxiv-2603-04125: Berti and others present a baseline and benchmark for few-shot open-set action recognition. Few-shot action recognition shows promise but often assumes a closed set, failing in real open-set settings, while image recognition is shown but video remains underexplored. Their extension adapts a Feature-Residual Discriminator from skeletons to video. Experiments on five data show common methods give marginal gains, while their discriminator enhances unknown rejection while keeping closed-set score intact, setting a new state of the art. Website, code, and benchmark are ready.
arxiv-2603-04325: Ruck and colleagues judge whether synthetic image edits look real enough to test AI. They add fog, rain, snow, and night to car camera images from 40 clear day photos. Rule libraries face generative editors, scored by a vision language jury and by embedding comparison with real bad weather images. Generative methods win big: the best tops the best rule method by about 3.6 times on acceptance. Fog is easiest, night hardest, and top generative work matches or beats real images on most conditions.
arxiv-2603-04425: Sabahat and Khan analyze a multigenerational cellular network dataset from OpenCelliD for strategic planning. Mobile data growth demands smart infrastructure management for quality of service and efficiency. Their study covers 1,818 towers, mostly LTE, across three countries, concentrated in Pakistan. Legacy 2G and 3G gear persists in major cities, many towers sit underused, and non-4G demand zones leave active users on outdated technology. A new signal density metric separates absolute overuse from local congestion. Results guide operators on LTE upgrades, resource allocation, and bridging gaps in underserved regions.
arxiv-2603-04725: Toniato presents a holo QCD model for quarkonium melting in this MSc thesis. The AdS/CFT link frames strongly coupled gauge laws and deep QCD effects. A self-made active model in the EMD framework studies meson mass spectra and melting. Finite heat work reveals a shift from lockup to freedom plus stepwise quark-state melting. At finite density, rising chem push speeds meson melting, with spectral functions changing smoothly. A curved Born-Infeld-dilaton model shows magnet fields shifting inverse magnet speedup to magnet speedup.
arxiv-2603-04925: Sebastian Heineking and team study whether advertisements blended into retrieval-augmented making replies can be detected on its own. They build a taxonomy of advertising styles from explicitness and appeal type, simulate advertisers changing styles to evade finding, and test detector toughness under those shifts. Entity-spotting models that pinpoint ads exactly prove highly strong and largely robust to style changes. Lightweight models like random forests and SVMs, suited to low-resource devices, prove brittle instead, pointing to a need for leanness-oriented research.
arxiv-2603-05125: Louis Depaepe and team study with numbers a flat exciton-polariton fluid in nonlinear motion driven by two counter-propagating laser beams. With a driven-dissipative Gross-Pitaevskii method, they spot four regimes from pump strength, laser detuning, and injected momentum: linear, solitonic, turbulent, and superfluid. The turbulent zone is wide and well-set, marked by self-starting vortex nucleation and reduced time coherence. Phase diagrams mark shifts between regimes and paths linking the four behaviors, and the turbulent zone holds up over realistic GaAs micro-cavity settings.
arxiv-2603-05225: Deming Chen and team lay out a ten-year AI-hardware co-design roadmap, as the two paths intertwine inseparably. Fragmentation blocks adaptive systems across cloud, edge, and real settings, with progress hinging on intelligence per joule. The roadmap redefines scaling through leanness, joining, and cross-layer tuning across algorithms and designs. Success means a thousandfold leanness gain for training and inference, plus energy-aware self-optimizing cloud, edge, and real AI systems. It also means wider infrastructure access and human-centric design, via coordinated national and public-private initiatives.
arxiv-2603-05325: Syver Døving Agdestein and Benjamin Sanderse test symmetry for large-eddy closures. Three share a Galilean-invariant build: perceptron, group-convolutional and tensor-basis networks. Uniform grids reduce the group to the octahedral group. Across sizes all three level off at the same scores and floor. Tensor-basis and equivariant models match this floor using 25 times fewer settings. Trained across viscosities with filter-scale Reynolds number input, they generalize. They hold dissipation tuning at held-out values, partly correcting Taylor-Green flow. Reynolds-number generalization is largely that.
arxiv-2603-05525: Sanjanasri and team survey molecular representations for chemistry that borrow from NLP and serve chemical data work. Deep learning's spread into the natural sciences created a need for molecular forms readable by machines and clear to scientists across fields. The paper presents popular forms of this kind and covers notable AI uses with them. It aims as a guide for new workers in chemical representations working at the chemistry and materials meeting point.
arxiv-2603-05625: Choi and team look at guarding against data-tamper attacks by studying the foe, not the attack itself. They present a framework for naming foe traits from an observed attack. Lacking extra knowledge, the foe cannot be named, since several foes could produce the same observed attack. A field-free framework then names the most likely foe. Foe knowledge aids defense twice: it enables fixes outside the learning code or limits foe power. It also improves defense methods that hit learning head-on, such as hostile rule-setting.
arxiv-2603-06025: Larooij views intent clearing up through the open search frame, where users transform gut or aware needs into formal ones. Boosting clearing up with search can lift scores where models lack built-in knowledge. In touchy domains like healthcare, state, legal scenes, data stores may hold guarded information. The paper explores a search-boosted agent as go-between, guard for touchy sets. Tackling this needs knowing what is guarded and against what. The approach proceeds in three steps: define an attack model, design defenses, build testing methods for the tradeoff.
arxiv-2603-06125: Sivy and Strecka study a bendable spin-1/2 Ising chain under longitudinal or transverse fields. Its magnetoelastic coupling is tied straight to lattice distortion. With harmonic and static adiabatic approximations, they work out the Gibbs free energy exactly by transfer-matrix and Jordan-Wigner. They pick the least distortion. A longitudinal field gives sharp thermal jumps ending at a critical point, with metastable states and hysteresis when cold. A transverse field gives a smooth quantum change at zero temperature, with susceptibility growing without bound and compressibility falling to nil.
arxiv-2603-06325: Pennington and his team use tensor network approximate quantum compiling for shallow circuits of 18 to 39 CNOT depth. The circuits prepare 100 site Heisenberg chain ground states with alternating bonds and spin-1/2, in both topological phases, at 97.9 percent fidelity or better. On IBM hardware, the states show all key signatures of symmetry protected order. These include non local string order up to length 20, entanglement spectrum degeneracies, and edge modes. Together, these independent diagnostics show current quantum machines as platforms for large scale such matter studies.
arxiv-2603-06525: Wagner and Yim present an underactuated monopedal robot that rolls and jumps, for multimodal locomotion on low-gravity bodies, using only two reaction wheels for spatial orientation. Two controllers aim the jump direction on the ground and the leg for landing after flight: a balancing controller and an aerial reorientation controller. They demonstrate rolling, targeted jumps with landings, and self-righting with only three actuators total, at 0.33 metres, with simple mode switching handling varied landscapes and conditions.
arxiv-2603-06625: Yu and Gao tackle incomplete pavement condition data, where sensor errors and uneven checks leave gaps that bias repair decisions, especially when gaps are systematic. They use a joint learning-based Graph Convolutional Network that learns missing values from adjacent-section features and links between observed states, catching nearby-section ties other graph neural network kinds miss. In a Texas Department of Transportation Austin District case study, the model produces good imputation results. It offers agencies usable road estimates from partial networks rather than dropping gap records.
arxiv-2603-06725: Dovale-Farelo and Choudhary assess how to predict Schottky barrier heights at silicon-metal interfaces, a key step for charge injection in devices. They test several exchange-correlation treatments against three bulk-check plans on silicon-metal cases, then benchmark against lab data. The main driver of accuracy is match between interface and bulk-check work in shape and electrostatics. Mixed hybrid-semilocal methods with strained bulk checks give near-lab accuracy at modest cost.
arxiv-2603-06825: Miserev and colleagues reply to a comment by Belitz and Kirkpatrick on their article about instability in ferromagnetic quantum criticality. The original article treats ground-state symmetry in electron gases in two and three dimensions with varied spin-orbit splitting. A reply of this kind answers points raised by critics and states where the authors stand on disputed claims. Readers tracking the debate should read the reply alongside the comment and the original article to see where agreement ends and dispute remains.
arxiv-2603-07225: Correa and colleagues prove a log Bott local rule for global smooth sections of the log tangent bundle on a compact complex space with simple normal crossings divisor. Unlike classical versions, the zero scheme may have non-isolated compact components. Those components must be local complete intersections satisfying a natural Bott nondegeneracy condition. They also give a current-theory form and, in the local complete meeting case, name the local residue term with a Coleff-Herrera current.
arxiv-2603-08025: Mokhtar and colleagues tackle the measurement load of hybrid quantum-classical methods for electronic structure, where large Hamiltonians demand many measurements. Their framework drives the Hamiltonian toward a block-diagonal form in the Slater-determinant basis through sequential Givens rotations. Rather than tuning a wave function, it transforms the Hamiltonian itself, with rotation angles set from small blocks by classical means. That keeps quantum work to a small fixed set of measurements per step. Angle-merging trims circuit depth; tests cover nitrogen and hydrogen systems.
arxiv-2603-08625: Cárcamo Hernández and colleagues build an inverse seesaw model on a Delta-27 symmetry plus Abelian discrete symmetries. The symmetry breaking pattern yields mass hierarchies and mixing angles that fit the cobimaximal pattern. Leptogenesis in the model explains the observed matter excess across a wide range, but only when neutrino masses follow the normal order.
arxiv-2603-08725: Luigi Capogrosso and colleagues survey ultra-low-power edge AI processors and bench three head to head. They sort commercial and research chips by compute style, power budget, and memory shape for always-on work. On a 336-million-operation segmentation model, the in-sensor Sony chip leads on utilization and energy-delay. The GAP9 leads on energy within microcontroller budgets, and the STM32N6 is fastest at a higher energy cost.
arxiv-2603-08825: Jay Revolinsky and colleagues build discrete graphs with local message passing alone, no global attention. Their GenGNN backbone keeps edge fields alive while refining coupled node-edge states in latent space. Diffusion models built on it clear a 90 percent pass rate on standard tests, run up to five times faster than transformer rivals, and resist over-smoothing while cleaning up.
arxiv-2603-09525: Nicola D. Kelly and colleagues report the bulk magnetic properties of lanthanide tantalates whose magnetic ions sit on a distorted square lattice. Powder neutron diffraction confirms the crystal structure for the terbium, holmium, and erbium members and fixes the magnetic structure of the terbium compound, which orders antiferromagnetically at low temperature. The dysprosium member may show short-range order, while holmium and erbium show correlations without ordering in range. Specific heat data point to a Kramers doublet ground state for erbium.
arxiv-2603-09625: Ümit Mert Çağlar and Alptekin Temizel ground synthetic data generation and scoring in vision and language models, for remote sensing. Usual metrics compare latent features, which are hard to read and weakly tied to downstream gains. Their framework joins generative models with segmentation and captioning tools. It yields ARAS400k, with 100k real and 300k synthetic images, each paired with maps and descriptions, so semantic composition and cross-modal consistency can be checked directly.
arxiv-2603-10225: Maxwell Miller-Golub and coauthors widen the harmonic loss for neural networks beyond plain Euclidean distance. Cross entropy training suffers weak interpretability and unbounded weight growth, while the harmonic alternative stays tied to one geometry. They test many distance metrics inside distance tailored harmonic losses on vision backbones and language models alike. Cosine distance gives the best overall trade, raising accuracy while lowering carbon emissions; other metrics sharpen interpretability.
arxiv-2603-10425: Boon Suan Ho proves a new lower bound for the kissing number in 19 dimensions, raising the known bound by a few hundred. The prior odd-sign construction of Cohn and Li turns the problem into finding a length 19 binary code with minimum distance 5 inside a punctured extended Golay code. In an explicit model of that ambient code, Ho isolates the words to avoid. A chosen subcode puts them in few cosets, and lifting an independent set there gives the needed nonlinear code.
arxiv-2603-10625: Yunkai Lou and co-authors present ExBI, a system for exploratory business intelligence built on a hypergraph data model. Analysts now work in rounds, refining questions as they go, while older systems lean on expert knowledge, cost a lot, and keep static schemas. ExBI adds Source, Join, and View operators for dynamic schema change and view reuse, plus sampling with provable estimation guarantees. On LDBC data it ran far faster than Neo4j and MySQL baselines, with a small average counting error.
arxiv-2603-10725: Artem Dvirniak and co-authors propose HIR-SDD, a speech deepfake detection framework that reasons in a human-inspired way. Modern audio models let adversaries impersonate people to gain access to private information. Current detectors generalize poorly to new domains and generators, and explain little. Their framework pairs large audio language models with chain-of-thought reasoning drawn from a new human-annotated dataset. In tests the system classified clips well and gave plain, human-perceptible reasons for calling a clip bona fide or spoof.
arxiv-2603-10825: Wai Ip Chu and co-authors present MEDISEG, a dataset of medication images with masks marking each pill, aimed at preventing adverse drug events. Medication errors often start with trouble identifying pills in real settings, and older datasets rarely show overlap or blocked views. MEDISEG annotates dozens of pill types across thousands of images, from single pills to cluttered dosette boxes. YOLOv8 and YOLOv9 trained on it scored high on small and large subsets. Few-shot tests showed base training sharply improved recognition of new pill classes.
arxiv-2603-10925: Oleg Kuliashov and coauthors model supercurrents in Josephson junctions. The normal region of these junctions is coated with chiral molecules. They ask whether molecular handedness leaves a mark on the current. They use a Bogoliubov-de Gennes tight-binding model. In symmetric, zero-field setups, the charge current-phase relation barely responds to chirality. The spin-polarized current answers strongly by contrast. It also answers anisotropically. Opposite enantiomers give distinct signals. Those signals persist well below the critical temperature. They can be boosted by tuning molecular orientation.
arxiv-2603-11225: A. S. Joglekar and A. G. R. Thomas simulate how a large-amplitude electron plasma wave evolves when collisions are weak, with electrons bouncing in the wave faster than they collide. Their Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck runs show three phases: a short trapping phase with minimal collisional effect, a long detrapping phase where collisions matter most, and a short final Landau damping phase. During detrapping the frequency shift grows away from the linear root, and they fit damping rates, shift growth, and wave lifetimes against collision frequency, wavenumber, and amplitude.
arxiv-2603-11425: Hain, Lerner, and Manning ask whether the tools used for passive solids can predict where an active solid will deform. Passive disordered solids hold local weak spots that steer later plastic change. The team studies dense packs of self-propelled rods, a simple active material. They extend the idea of local excitations to landscapes that include active, non-conservative forces. Force-based cubic excitations then flag future plastic events well, a step toward control of active solids.
arxiv-2603-11825: Diamantopoulos and co-authors ask whether X-ray power spectrum shapes in AGN change with photon energy. They use two restless low-mass Seyfert galaxies, NGC4051 and NGC4395, as test cases. Power spectra in six bands from 0.3 to 20 keV, from XMM-Newton, Suzaku, and NuSTAR archives, all fit a bending power-law model. Spectra from different satellites and epochs agree, so the flickering process looks steady. The bend frequency stays put across energies, the high-frequency slope flattens at higher energies, and the amplitude drops.
arxiv-2603-12125: Southworth measures the twin F-type stars of the eclipsing binary BS Draconis. TESS watched the system for 40 sectors, and published spectra add the motion side. The two F3 V stars are near twins on a 3.36 day circular orbit. Their masses and radii now carry small errors, and the primary eclipse is pinned down at last. The hotter star is also the larger and heavier one, by a slight but firm margin. Eclipse timing is so steady the pair may serve as a celestial clock.
arxiv-2603-12225: Rubinstein-Salzedo and Zhou study the evil twin property in sums of wildflower games. A game has this property when a twin form swaps its misère and normal outcome classes. Sums of wildflowers, games built in a two-part form, are their test bed. A large closed set of such sums proves to have the property. The proof extends misère genus theory toward partizan games. Mutant flower sums form the largest such closed set, and finding their outcome class is NP-hard.
arxiv-2603-12325: Adamczyk, Kamoski, and Kulkarni solve maximum entropy exploration without any rollouts. Good exploration policies spread visits evenly across the state space in the long run. Most methods estimate visit counts from repeated on-policy rollouts, which costs heavy compute. Their intrinsic reward comes from the visit spread itself, inside an average-reward frame. A spectral route reads the stationary spread from dominant eigenvectors of a transition matrix. The EVE algorithm then iterates like a value method, with proven convergence and strong grid-world results.
arxiv-2603-12425: Lukyanenko and Vandehey give a proof of Lagrange's theorem for continued fractions, then extend it widely. Finite expansions mark the fractions, and ones that turn periodic mark quadratic roots in the classic case. Their frame covers Iwasawa fractions in real, complex, 3D, quaternionic, octonionic, and Heisenberg forms. Finite form, a modular group test, and a parabolic fixed point prove the same. Periodic points match loxodromic fixed points and quadratic roots through Clifford algebra. Nearest-integer and Hurwitz fractions gain new proofs along the way.
arxiv-2603-12625: Ty Valencia and co-authors rethink multimodal recommendation as a question of semantic space, not just feature fusion. Raw image features track how items look, while users choose by style, material, and use context. Their VLM4Rec uses a large vision-language model to turn each item image into a plain language description. Those grounded semantics become dense item vectors for matching user profiles.
